Σκευᾶς, -ᾶ Sceva: [[acts 19 14|Act.19:14.]]† (AS)
σκευή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: 3Ma.5:45 R * ;] equipment, tackle: [[acts 27 19|Act.27:19.]]† (AS)

σκεῦος, -ους, τό [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;] a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, see MM, xxii): [[mark 11 16|Mrk.11:16]], [[luke 8 16|Luk.8:16]], [[john 19 29|Jhn.19:29]], [[acts 10 11|Act.10:11, 16 11:5]], [[romans 9 21|Rom.9:21]], [[revelation 18 12|Rev.18:12]]; pl., [[2-timothy 2 20|2Ti.2:20]], [[revelation 2 27|Rev.2:27]]; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, [[hebrews 9 21|Heb.9:21;]] pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, [[matthew 12 29|Mat.12:29]], [[mark 3 27|Mrk.3:27]], [[luke 17 31|Luk.17:31]]; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., [[acts 27 17|Act.27:17.]] Metaphorical, of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, [[acts 9 15|Act.9:15;]] ὀργῆς, [[romans 9 22|Rom.9:22;]] ἐλέους, [[romans 9 23|Rom.9:23;]] σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. [[romans 9 21|Rom.9:21]]), [[2-timothy 2 21|2Ti.2:21]]; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., [[1-peter 3 7|1Pe.3:7;]] so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., [[1-thessalonians 4 4|1Th.4:4]] (but see infr.); of the body, [[2-corinthians 4 7|2Co.4:7;]] so perh. [[1-thessalonians 4 4|1Th.4:4]] (but see supr., and see: κτάομαι).† κτάομαι, -ῶμαι [in LXX chiefly for קָנָה ;] in pres., impf., fut. and aor., to procure for oneself, get, gain, acquire (the pf. and plpf., to have acquired, hence to possess, do not occur in NT): with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 10 9|Mat.10:9]], [[luke 18 12|Luk.18:12]], [[acts 8 20|Act.8:20]]; with genitive pret., [[acts 22 28|Act.22:28;]] ἐκ with genitive pret., [[acts 1 18|Act.1:18;]] τ,ψυχὰς ὑμῶν (MM, xvi), [[luke 21 19|Luk.21:19;]] τ. ἑαυτοῦ σκεῦος κτᾶσθαι, [[1-thessalonians 4 4|1Th.4:4]] (where if σ. = body, κ. must = pf., κέκτημαι; see MM, xvi; M, Th., in l; Field, Notes, 72 f. But σ. is most frequently taken as = wife; see Thayer, see word; Lft., Notes, 53 ff.; ICC, in l).† (AS)

σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;] a tent, booth, tabernacle: [[matthew 17 4|Mat.17:4]], [[mark 9 5|Mrk.9:5]], [[luke 9 33|Luk.9:33]], [[hebrews 11 9|Heb.11:9]]; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., [[luke 16 9|Luk.16:9;]] of the Mosaic tabernacle, [[hebrews 8 5|Heb.8:5 9:2-3, 6 9:8, 21]]; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, [[acts 7 44|Act.7:44;]] of its heavenly prototype, [[hebrews 8 2|Heb.8:2 9:11]], [[revelation 13 6|Rev.13:6 15:5 21:3]]; of the temple, [[hebrews 13 10|Heb.13:10;]] ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, [[acts 7 43|Act.7:43]] (LXX); metaphorically, ἡ σ. Δαυείδ [[acts 15 16|Act.15:16]] (LXX).† (AS)

σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ (σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכָּה, [[deuteronomy 16 16|Deu.16:16 31:10]], [[zechariah 14 16|Zec.14:16, 18-19]]; I [[esther 5 51|Est.5:51]], 1Ma.10:21, 2Ma.1:9 2Mac 1:18 * ;] prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, [[leviticus 23 34|Lev.23:34]], al.; see Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: [[john 7 2|Jhn.7:2.]]† (AS)
σκηνοποιός, -όν (σκηνή, ποιέω), making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: [[acts 18 3|Act.18:3.]]† (AS)
σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;] = σκηνή, a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: [[2-corinthians 5 1|2Co.5:1 5:4]].† (AS)

σκηνόω, -ῶ (σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַן ;] to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), [[revelation 7 15|Rev.7:15;]] before ἐν, with dative of person(s), [[john 1 14|Jhn.1:14;]] id. with dative loc., [[revelation 12 12|Rev.12:12 13:6]]; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), [[revelation 21 3|Rev.21:3]] (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).† (AS)

σκήνωμα, -τος, τό (σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;] a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling ([[psalms 132 5|Psa.132:5]], al.), [[acts 7 46|Act.7:46]]. Metaphorical, of the body: [[2-peter 1 13|2Pe.1:13-14.]]† (AS)

σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for צֵל, 4Ki.20:9 ff., [[psalms 57 1|Psa.57:1]], al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, [[job 3 5|Job.3:5]], [[psalms 3 4|Psa.3:4]], [[isaiah 9 2|Isa.9:2]] (1) (see ICC, in l), al. ;] 1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: [[mark 4 32|Mrk.4:32]], [[acts 5 15|Act.5:15]]; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, [[matthew 4 16|Mat.4:16]], [[luke 1 79|Luk.1:79]]" (LXX) . 2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., [[hebrews 8 5|Heb.8:5;]] opposite to σῶμα, [[colossians 2 17|Col.2:17;]] opposite to εἰκών, [[hebrews 10 1|Heb.10:1.]]† (AS)
σκιρτάω, -ῶ [in LXX: [[genesis 25 22|Gen.25:22]] (רָצַץ hithpo.), [[psalms 114 4|Psa.114:4]], 6 (רָקַד), etc. ;] to leap: [[luke 1 41|Luk.1:41, 44 6:23]].† (AS)

σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ (σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 10 16|Deu.10:16]], [[jeremiah 4 4|Jer.4:4]] (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) * ;] hardness of heart: [[matthew 19 8|Mat.19:8]], [[mark 10 5|Mrk.10:5 16:14]].† (AS)

σκληρός, -ά, -όν (σκέλλω, to dry), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה ;] hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opposite to μαλακός); metaphorically, in various uses; (a) of men, hard, stern, severe: [[matthew 25 24|Mat.25:24;]] (b) of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), [[acts 26 14|Act.26:14;]] λόγος, [[john 6 60|Jhn.6:60;]] ἄνεμος, [[james 3 4|Jas.3:4;]] σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.† SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v (AS)
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ (σκληρός), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 9 27|Deu.9:27]] (קְשִׁי), etc. ;] hardness; metaphorically, of stubbornness: [[romans 2 5|Rom.2:5.]]† (AS)
σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον (σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: [[exodus 33 3|Exo.33:3]], 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;] stiff-necked: metaphorically, [[acts 7 51|Act.7:51.]]† (AS)

σκληρύνω (σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה hi., also for חָזַק ;] to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), [[romans 9 18|Rom.9:18;]] T. καρδίας ([[psalms 95 8|Psa.95:8]]), [[hebrews 3 8|Heb.3:8, 15 4:7]]. Pass., to become hardened: [[acts 19 9|Act.19:9]], [[hebrews 3 13|Heb.3:13]].† (AS)

σκολιός, -ά, -όν [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 32 5|Deu.32:5]] (עִקֵּשׁ), [[proverbs 28 18|Pro.28:18]] (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דֶּרֶךְ עָקַשׁ), [[isaiah 40 4|Isa.40:4]] (עָקֹב), etc. ;] curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): [[luke 3 5|Luk.3:5]] (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: [[acts 2 40|Act.2:40]], [[philippians 2 15|Php.2:15]], [[1-peter 2 18|1Pe.2:18]].† (AS)

σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ [in LXX: [[numbers 33 55|Num.33:55]] (שֵׂךְ), [[hosea 2 6|Hos.2:6]] (8) (סִיר), [[ezekiel 28 24|Eze.28:24]] (סִלּוֹן), Sir.43:19 * ;] anything pointed, esp. 1. in cl., a stake 2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, [[2-corinthians 12 7|2Co.12:7]] (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).† (AS)

ακοπέω, -ῶ (σκοπός), [in LXX: [[esther 8 13|Est.8:13]], 2Ma.4:5 * ;] to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), [[2-corinthians 4 13|2Co.4:13]], [[philippians 2 4|Php.2:4]]; with accusative of person(s), [[romans 16 17|Rom.16:17]], [[philippians 3 17|Php.3:17]]; before μή, [[luke 11 35|Luk.11:35;]] σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), [[galatians 6 1|Gal.6:1]] (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).† SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω (AS)

σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה ;] 1. a watcher, watchman ([[ezekiel 3 17|Eze.3:17]], al.). 2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wis.5:12, 21, al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: [[philippians 3 14|Php.3:14.]]† (AS)

σκορπίζω [in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;] in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, [[john 10 12|Jhn.10:12;]] ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, [[matthew 12 30|Mat.12:30]], [[luke 11 23|Luk.11:23]]; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., [[john 16 32|Jhn.16:32;]] of one who dispenses blessings, [[2-corinthians 9 9|2Co.9:9]] (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).† (AS)
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for עַקְרָב ;] a scorpion: [[luke 10 19|Luk.10:19 11:12]], [[revelation 9 3|Rev.9:3, 5 9:10]] † (AS)
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν (σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;] dark: opposite to φωτεινός, [[matthew 6 23|Mat.6:23]], [[luke 11 34|Luk.11:34, 36]].† (AS)

σκοτία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: [[job 28 3|Job.28:3]] (אֹפֶל), [[micah 3 6|Mic.3:6]] (חָשַׁךְ), [[isaiah 16 3|Isa.16:3]] * ;] in late writers = σκότος, darkness: [[john 6 17|Jhn.6:17 20:1]]. Metaphorical, (a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): [[matthew 10 27|Mat.10:27]], [[luke 12 3|Luk.12:3]]; (b) of spiritual darkness: [[matthew 4 16|Mat.4:16]], [[john 1 5|Jhn.1:5 8:12 12:35, 40]], [[1-john 1 5|1Jn.1:5]] [[john 2 8|Jn 2:8-9]] [[john 2 11|Jn 2:11]].† (AS)

σκοτίζω (σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ ;] to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, [[matthew 24 29|Mat.24:29]], [[mark 13 24|Mrk.13:24]], [[luke 23 45|Luk.23:45]] (Rec., WH, mg.), [[revelation 8 12|Rev.8:12.]] Metaphorical, of the mind, [[romans 1 21|Rom.1:21 11:10]]" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).† (AS)
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό), darkness: [[hebrews 12 18|Heb.12:18]], Rec.† (AS)
σκοτόω, -ῶ (σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר ;] to darken: [[revelation 9 2|Rev.9:2 16:10]]. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., [[ephesians 4 18|Eph.4:18]] (cf. σκοτίζω).† (AS)
σκύβαλον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Sir.27:4 * ;] refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): [[philippians 3 8|Php.3:8.]]† (AS)
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: [[colossians 3 11|Col.3:11.]]† (AS)
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν) (σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: [[genesis 40 7|Gen.40:7]] (רַע), etc. ;] of a gloomy countenance: [[matthew 6 16|Mat.6:16]], [[luke 24 17|Luk.24:17]].† (AS)

σκύλλω 1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.). 2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), [[mark 5 35|Mrk.5:35]], [[luke 8 49|Luk.8:49]]; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, [[matthew 9 36|Mat.9:36;]] mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, [[luke 7 6|Luk.7:6]] (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).† (AS)
σκῦλον (Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;] mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: [[luke 11 22|Luk.11:22.]]† (AS)
σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον (σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω), eaten of worms: [[acts 12 23|Act.12:23]] (cf. 2Ma.9:9, and see MM, xxiii) † (AS)

σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;] a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, [[mark 9 48|Mrk.9:48]] (LXX, [[isaiah 66 24|Isa.66:24;]] cf. Sir.7:17, Jdth.16:17).† (AS)

σμαράγδινος (σμάραγδος, which see), 1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11). 2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: [[revelation 4 3|Rev.4:3]] (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).† (AS)

σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: [[exodus 28 9|Exo.28:9]] (שֹׁהַם) [[exodus 36 17|Exo.36:17]] ([[exodus 39 10|Exo.39:10]]) (בָּרֶקֶת), [[ezekiel 28 13|Eze.28:13]] (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;] emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): [[revelation 21 19|Rev.21:19.]]† (AS)
σμύρνα (in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;] myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: [[matthew 2 11|Mat.2:11]], [[john 19 39|Jhn.19:39]].† (AS)

Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 2:8]].† Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 2:8]] T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).† (AS)

Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 2:8]].† Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ, [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 2:8]] T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).† (AS)
σμυρνίζω (σιύρνα), 1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79). 2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., [[mark 15 23|Mrk.15:23.]]† (AS)

Σόδομα, -ων, τά (Heb. סְדֹם), Sodom ([[genesis 13 10|Gen.13:10, 12]], al.): [[matthew 10 15|Mat.10:15 11:23-24]] [[luke 10 12|Luk.10:12 17:29]], [[romans 9 29|Rom.9:29]]" (LXX), [[2-peter 2 6|2Pe.2:6]], Ju 7, [[revelation 11 8|Rev.11:8]].† (AS)

αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399). 1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, [[luke 5 37|Luk.5:37;]] αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, [[john 2 25|Jhn.2:25;]] αὐ.ὑμεῖς, [[john 3 28|Jhn.3:28;]] καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, [[romans 15 14|Rom.15:14;]] αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, [[john 2 24|Jhn.2:24;]] αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, [[mark 2 25|Mrk.2:25;]] ὑμεῖς αὐ., [[mark 6 31|Mrk.6:31;]] esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, [[matthew 3 4|Mat.3:4]], [[mark 6 17|Mrk.6:17]], [[john 16 27|Jhn.16:27]], [[1-thessalonians 3 11|1Th.3:11]], al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]] (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), [[matthew 1 21|Mat.1:21, 12:50]], [[luke 6 35|Luk.6:35]], al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), [[matthew 8 24|Mat.8:24]], [[mark 4 38|Mrk.4:38]], al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), [[matthew 14 2|Mat.14:2]], [[mark 14 15|Mrk.14:15, 44]], [[luke 1 22|Luk.1:22, 2:28]], al. 2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, [[matthew 7 9|Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44]], al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., [[matthew 9 18|Mat.9:18]], [[mark 13 1|Mrk.13:1]], al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. Heb. אֲשֶׁר לוֹ; WM, 184ff.; Bl., §50, 4; MM, see word), [[mark 7 25|Mrk.7:25]], [[revelation 3 8|Rev.3:8, 7:2]], al.; in constr. ad sensum, without proper subject expressly indicated, [[matthew 4 23|Mat.4:23]], [[acts 8 5|Act.8:5]], [[2-corinthians 2 13|2Co.2:13]], al.; genitive αὐτοῦ = ἐκείνου, [[romans 11 11|Rom.11:11]], [[1-thessalonians 2 19|1Th.2:19]], [[titus 3 5|Tit.3:5]], [[hebrews 2 4|Heb.2:4]]. 3. ὁ, ἡ, τὸ αὐ., the same: [[hebrews 1 12|Heb.1:12, 13:8]]; τὸ αὐ., ποιεῖν, [[matthew 5 46|Mat.5:46, 47]], al.; φρονεῖν, [[romans 12 16|Rom.12:16, 15:5]], [[philippians 2 2|Php.2:2]], al.; τὰ αὐ., [[acts 15 27|Act.15:27]], [[romans 2 1|Rom.2:1]], al.; κατὰ τὸ (τὰ) αὐ. (MM, see word), [[acts 14 1|Act.14:1]], [[luke 6 23|Luk.6:23]], al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), [[matthew 22 34|Mat.22:34]], [[acts 1 15|Act.1:15]], al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5, 12:11]]; with dative (cl.), [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5;]] with a noun, λόγος, [[mark 14 39|Mrk.14:39;]] μέτρος, [[philippians 1 30|Php.1:30;]] πνεῦμα, [[1-corinthians 12 4|1Co.12:4.]] (AS)

Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in [[acts 3 11|Act.3:11 5:12]]; in [[acts 7 47|Act.7:47]] T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: [[matthew 1 6|Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42]], [[luke 11 31|Luk.11:31 12:27]], [[john 10 23|Jhn.10:23]], [[acts 3 11|Act.3:11 5:12 7:47]].† (AS)

Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in [[acts 3 11|Act.3:11 5:12]]; in [[acts 7 47|Act.7:47]] T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה), Solomon: [[matthew 1 6|Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42]], [[luke 11 31|Luk.11:31 12:27]], [[john 10 23|Jhn.10:23]], [[acts 3 11|Act.3:11 5:12 7:47]].† (AS)
σορός, -οῦ, ἡ [in LXX: [[genesis 50 26|Gen.50:26]] (אָרוֹן), [[job 21 32|Job.21:32]] A * ;] (a) a cinerary urn (Hom.); (b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, a1.): [[luke 7 14|Luk.7:14.]]† (AS)

σός, -ή, -όν possess. prop. of second of person(s), thy, thine: [[matthew 7 3|Mat.7:3]], al.; as subst., οἱ σοί, thy kinsfolk, friends, [[mark 5 19|Mrk.5:19;]] τὸ σόν, what is thine, [[matthew 20 14|Mat.20:14 25:25]]; τὰ σά, thy goods, [[luke 6 30|Luk.6:30]] (AS)

αὐτός, -ή, -ό, determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399). 1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii); (1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, [[luke 5 37|Luk.5:37;]] αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, [[john 2 25|Jhn.2:25;]] αὐ.ὑμεῖς, [[john 3 28|Jhn.3:28;]] καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, [[romans 15 14|Rom.15:14;]] αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, [[john 2 24|Jhn.2:24;]] αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, [[mark 2 25|Mrk.2:25;]] ὑμεῖς αὐ., [[mark 6 31|Mrk.6:31;]] esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, [[matthew 3 4|Mat.3:4]], [[mark 6 17|Mrk.6:17]], [[john 16 27|Jhn.16:27]], [[1-thessalonians 3 11|1Th.3:11]], al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]] (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word); (2) emphatic, he, she, it (M, Pr., 86; Bl., §48, 1, 2, 7), [[matthew 1 21|Mat.1:21, 12:50]], [[luke 6 35|Luk.6:35]], al.; pointing to some one as master (cl.), [[matthew 8 24|Mat.8:24]], [[mark 4 38|Mrk.4:38]], al.; αὐ., καὶ αὐ. = οὗτος, ὁ δε (BL, §48, 1), [[matthew 14 2|Mat.14:2]], [[mark 14 15|Mrk.14:15, 44]], [[luke 1 22|Luk.1:22, 2:28]], al. 2. In oblique cases (cl.), for the simple pron. of 3rd of person(s), he, she, it, [[matthew 7 9|Mat.7:9, 10:12, 26:44]], al.; with ptcp. in genitive absol., [[matthew 9 18|Mat.9:18]], [[mark 13 1|Mrk.13:1]], al. (for irreg. constructions, V. Bl., §74, 5); pleonastically after the relative (cf. (MM, see word), [[acts 14 1|Act.14:1]], [[luke 6 23|Luk.6:23]], al.; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐ., together (MM, see word), [[matthew 22 34|Mat.22:34]], [[acts 1 15|Act.1:15]], al.; ἓν κ. τὸ αὐ., [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5, 12:11]]; with dative (cl.), [[1-corinthians 11 5|1Co.11:5;]] with a noun, λόγος, [[mark 14 39|Mrk.14:39;]] μέτρος, [[philippians 1 30|Php.1:30;]] πνεῦμα, [[1-corinthians 12 4|1Co.12:4.]] (AS)
σουδάριον, -ου, τό(Lat.), handkerchief, kerchief: [[luke 19 20|Luk.19:20]], [[acts 19 12|Act.19:12]]; used as a head covering for the dead, [[john 11 44|Jhn.11:44 20:7]] (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).† (AS)
Σουσάννα, -ης (cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.) Susanna: [[luke 8 3|Luk.8:3.]]† (AS)

σοφία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חׇכְמָה ;] skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense; (a) of human wisdom: [[1-corinthians 2 1|1Co.2:1 2:4-5]], [[james 3 15|Jas.3:15]], [[revelation 13 18|Rev.13:18 17:9]]; σ. Σολομῶνος, [[matthew 12 42|Mat.12:42]], [[luke 11 31|Luk.11:31]]; Αἰγυπτίων, [[acts 7 22|Act.7:22;]] Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, [[1-corinthians 1 22|1Co.1:22;]] σ. λόγου, [[1-corinthians 1 17|1Co.1:17;]] τ. σοφῶν, [[1-corinthians 1 19|1Co.1:19]] (LXX); τ. κόσμου, [[1-corinthians 1 20|1Co.1:20-21 3:19]]; ἀνθρωπίνη, [[1-corinthians 2 13|1Co.2:13;]] σαρκική, [[2-corinthians 1 12|2Co.1:12;]] of wisdom in spiritual things: [[luke 21 15|Luk.21:15]], [[acts 6 3|Act.6:3, 10 7:10]], [[1-corinthians 2 6|1Co.2:6]], [[colossians 1 28|Col.1:28 2:23 3:16 4:5]], [[james 1 5|Jas.1:5 3:13, 17]], [[2-peter 3 15|2Pe.3:15]]; λόγος σοφίας, [[1-corinthians 12 8|1Co.12:8;]] πνεῦμα σοφίας, [[ephesians 1 17|Eph.1:17;]] σ. καὶ φρόνησις, [[ephesians 1 8|Eph.1:8;]] σ. καὶ σύνεσις, [[colossians 1 9|Col.1:9;]] (b) of divine wisdom: of God, [[romans 11 33|Rom.11:33]], [[1-corinthians 1 21|1Co.1:21 1:24 2:7]], [[revelation 7 12|Rev.7:12]]; πολυποίκιλος, [[ephesians 3 10|Eph.3:10]] of Christ, [[matthew 13 54|Mat.13:54]], [[mark 6 2|Mrk.6:2]], [[luke 2 40|Luk.2:40, 52]], [[1-corinthians 1 30|1Co.1:30]] [[colossians 2 3|Col.2:3]], [[revelation 5 12|Rev.5:12]]; of wisdom personified, [[matthew 11 19|Mat.11:19]], [[luke 7 35|Luk.7:35 11:49]].† SYN.: σύνεσις, intelligence; φρόνησις, prudence, which with σ. make up (Arist., N. Eth., i, 13) the three intellectual ἀρεταί. σ. is wisdom primary and absolute; in distinction from which φ. is practical, σύνεσις critical, both being applications of σ. in detail (cf. Lft., and ICC on [[colossians 1 9|Col.1:9;]] Lft., Notes, 317 f.; Tr., Syn., § LXXv; Cremer, 870 ff.). (AS)

σοφίζω (σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), [[2-timothy 3 15|2Ti.3:15]] (cf. [[psalms 19 8|Psa.19:8]] ([[psalms 119 98|Psa.119:98]]). As depon., -ομαι; (a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 ([[1-kings 5 11|3Ki.5:11]]), [[ecclesiastes 2 15|Ecc.2:15]], and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.); (b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., [[2-peter 1 16|2Pe.1:16]] (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).† (AS)

σοφός, -ή, -όν [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;] skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: [[romans 16 19|Rom.16:19]], [[1-corinthians 3 10|1Co.3:10]]; of the learned, [[romans 1 14|Rom.1:14, 22]], [[1-corinthians 1 19|1Co.1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20]]; of Jewish teachers, [[matthew 11 25|Mat.11:25]], [[luke 10 21|Luk.10:21]]; Christian, [[matthew 23 34|Mat.23:34;]] of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, [[1-corinthians 6 5|1Co.6:5]], [[ephesians 5 15|Eph.5:15]], [[james 3 13|Jas.3:13]]; of God, [[romans 16 27|Rom.16:27;]] compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, [[1-corinthians 1 25|1Co.1:25.]]† SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (see: σοφία, SYN.) (AS)
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ (= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here), Spain: [[romans 15 24|Rom.15:24, 28]].† (AS)

σπαράσσω [in LXX: [[2-samuel 22 8|2Ki.22:8]] B (גָּעַשׁ hith.), [[john 4 19|Jhn.4:19]] (הָמָה) Dan LXX 8:7 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), 3Ma.4:6 * ;] 1. to tear, rend, mangle. 2. to convulse: [[mark 1 26|Mrk.1:26]] (see Swete, in l) [[mark 9 26|Mrk.9:26]], [[luke 9 39|Luk.9:39]] (cf. συν-σπαράσσω).† (AS)

σπαργανόω, -ῶ (σπάργανον, a swathing-band) [in LXX: [[job 38 9|Job.38:9]], [[ezekiel 16 4|Eze.16:4]] (חָתַל pu.)* ;] to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: [[luke 2 7|Luk.2:7, 12]] (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).† (AS)

σπαταλάω, -ῶ (σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Sir.27:13 *), [in LXX: [[ezekiel 16 49|Eze.16:49]] (שָׁקַט hi.), Sir.21:15 * ;] to live riotously: [[1-timothy 5 6|1Ti.5:6]], [[james 5 5|Jas.5:5]] (Polyb.).† SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv) (AS)
σπάω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַף, ;] in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157), to draw: μάχαιραν, [[mark 14 47|Mrk.14:47]], [[acts 16 27|Act.16:27]],† (AS)

σπείρω [in LXX chiefly for זָרַע ;] to sow (seed): absol., [[matthew 6 26|Mat.6:26 13:3-4, 18 25:24, 26]], [[mark 4 3|Mrk.4:3-4]], [[luke 8 5|Luk.8:5 12:24]], [[john 4 36|Jhn.4:36]], [[2-corinthians 9 10|2Co.9:10]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 13 24|Mat.13:24, 27 13:37, 39]], [[mark 4 32|Mrk.4:32]], [[luke 8 5|Luk.8:5]], [[1-corinthians 15 36|1Co.15:36-37]]; before εἰς, [[matthew 13 22|Mat.13:22]], [[mark 4 18|Mrk.4:18]]; ἐν, [[matthew 13 24|Mat.13:24, 31]]; ἐπί, with genitive, [[mark 4 31|Mrk.4:31;]] ἐπί, with accusative, [[matthew 13 20|Mat.13:20, 23]], [[mark 4 16|Mrk.4:16, 20]]; παρά, with accusative, [[matthew 13 19|Mat.13:19.]] Metaphorical: [[1-corinthians 9 11|1Co.9:11 15:42-44]], [[galatians 6 7|Gal.6:7-8]], [[james 3 18|Jas.3:18]]; in proverbial sayings, [[matthew 25 24|Mat.25:24, 26]], [[luke 19 21|Luk.19:21-22]], [[john 4 37|Jhn.4:37]], [[2-corinthians 9 6|2Co.9:6]], [[galatians 6 7|Gal.6:7]]; in interpretation of parables, [[matthew 13 19|Mat.13:19-23]] [[mark 4 14|Mrk.4:14-20]] † (AS)

σπεύδω [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi., also for בָּהַל pi., hi., etc. ;] 1. most frequently intrans., to hasten: with inf. σπήλαιον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;] a cave, cavern: [[john 11 38|Jhn.11:38]], [[hebrews 11 38|Heb.11:38]], [[hebrews 6 15|Heb.6:15]]; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν ([[john 7 11|Jhn.7:11]]), [[matthew 21 13|Mat.21:13]], [[mark 11 17|Mrk.11:17]], [[luke 19 46|Luk.19:46]].† (AS)

σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ (on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41), 1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.). 2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).† (AS)
σπιλόω [in LXX: Wis.15:4 * ;] to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, [[james 3 6|Jas.3:6]], Ju 23.† (AS)

σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ 1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.). 2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically, (a) of moral blemish: [[ephesians 5 27|Eph.5:27]] (b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): [[2-peter 2 13|2Pe.2:13.]]† (AS)

σπλαγχνίζομαι (σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): [[proverbs 17 5|Pro.17:5]] A, 2Ma.6:8 (= -εύω) * ;] to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., [[luke 10 33|Luk.10:33 15:20]]; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., [[matthew 18 27|Mat.18:27 20:34]], [[mark 1 41|Mrk.1:41]]; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), [[matthew 14 14|Mat.14:14]], [[luke 7 13|Luk.7:13]]; ἐπί, with accusative, [[matthew 15 32|Mat.15:32]], [[mark 6 34|Mrk.6:34 8:2 9:22]]; ωερί, [[matthew 9 36|Mat.9:36.]] (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: [[1-kings 23 21|1Ki.23:21]], [[ezekiel 24 21|Eze.24:21]], Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on [[philippians 1 8|Php.1:8]], in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) † (AS)

σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, [in LXX: [[proverbs 12 10|Pro.12:10]] (רַחַם, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, [[psalms 25 6|Psa.25:6 40:12]] and by ἔλεος, [[isaiah 47 6|Isa.47:6]]), [[proverbs 26 22|Pro.26:22]] (בֶּטֶן), Wis.10:5, Sir.30:7, 2Ma.9:5 (6), al. ;] the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): [[acts 1 18|Act.1:18.]] Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on [[philippians 1 8|Php.1:8]]): [[2-corinthians 6 12|2Co.6:12 7:15]], Phm 7 12 20, [[1-john 3 17|1Jn.3:17]]; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, [[colossians 3 12|Col.3:12;]] σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, [[philippians 2 1|Php.2:1;]] σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, [[luke 1 78|Luk.1:78;]] σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, [[philippians 1 8|Php.1:8.]]† (AS)
σπόγγος, -ου, ὁ a sponge: [[matthew 27 48|Mat.27:48]], [[mark 15 36|Mrk.15:36]], [[john 19 29|Jhn.19:29]].† (AS)
